'''Cork City Football Club ''' is an [[List of association football clubs in the Republic of Ireland|Irish association football club]] based in [[Cork (city)|Cork]]. The club was founded and elected to the [[League of Ireland]] in [[1984–85 League of Ireland|1984]].

Cork City was one of the first clubs in Ireland (and the first in Cork) to field a team of professional footballers. With the progression of professionalism at the club, continued development of the [[Turners Cross (stadium)|Turners Cross stadium]] and the transition to summer football, the club became one of the biggest and best supported clubs in the country.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://archives.tcm.ie/businesspost/2008/08/17/story35159.asp | publisher= Sunday Business Post | title= Eircom League rocked by Cork City's financial difficulties | date= 17 August 2008 |quote="''Cork City is one of the biggest and best supported teams in the league''" |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081029131342/http://archives.tcm.ie/businesspost/2008/08/17/story35159.asp | archive-date= 29 October 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40828484.html | publisher = Irish Examiner | website = irishexaminer.com | title = Cork City games among biggest crowds of opening league rounds | date = 14 March 2022 | access-date = 26 March 2022 | archive-date = 26 March 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220326130301/https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40828484.html | url-status = live }}</ref> In a survey published in 2020, the club was the highest supported League of Ireland (LOI) club.<ref name="ITsurvey">{{cite news |last1=Malone |first1=Emmet |title=Football fan survey: Man United still top league among Irish fans |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/football-fan-survey-man-united-still-top-league-among-irish-fans-1.4185728 |newspaper=The Irish Times |access-date=16 February 2021 |date=29 February 2020 |archive-date=29 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129112901/https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/football-fan-survey-man-united-still-top-league-among-irish-fans-1.4185728 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Cork City won its third [[League of Ireland Premier Division|LOI Premier Division]] title, and first [[FAI Cup]] double, during the [[2017 League of Ireland Premier Division|2017 season]]. In September 2026, the club secured promotion from the [[League of Ireland First Division|First Division]] to the Premier Division, the third such promotion in six years.{{fact|date=September 2026}}

The club's traditional colours are green and white with red trim, and the crest is a variant of the Cork coat of arms. City's home games are played at [[Turners Cross (stadium)|Turners Cross]]."}}
